thread:
Priya (Support): heads-up — customer CTX-4918 is seeing a bunch of 502s when they hit what should be a 429 rate limit. They expect 429 for quota denies but our API returns 502/500 intermittently. Repro from their side attached. Request-id: req_0a9f3c.

Priya (Support): curl they used:
```bash
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \n  -d '{"input":"test"}' \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?model=gpt-medium\n```
Response sample:
```json
{
  "error": "Upstream error",
  "code": 502,
  "request_id": "req_0a9f3c"
}
```

Priya (Support): Customer says it correlates with bursty requests and when token refresh/quotas happen. Filing internal ticket: INC-2026. They're worried about billing and downstream retry storms.

Marco (Runtime): :eyes: I can see 502s from quota-gateway in our traces around that req id. Looks like quota-service timed out and the gateway returns a 502 instead of mapping to 429.

Alex (SRE): tagging @oncall-sre — throwing to SRE for immediate mitigation. Any chance this is the same dependency timeout regression we saw last week?

oncall-sre: I'm on it. Pulling logs and current circuit state.

Marco (Runtime): logs (tail):
```
2026-03-15T09:12:03Z quota-gateway trace=req_0a9f3c calling quota-service
2026-03-15T09:12:03Z quota-service WARNING slow request, 5.2s
2026-03-15T09:12:08Z quota-gateway ERROR dependency timeout -> upstream 502 returned to client
2026-03-15T09:12:08Z quota-gateway debug mapping not applied: classifier rule missing for auth_denied -> should map -> 429
```

Marco (Runtime): looks like two problems: 1) quota-service spike/latency (timeouts), 2) mapping layer in quota-gateway that translates quota responses to HTTP 4xx is failing to apply for some auth-deny flows, falling through to generic 502.

Priya (Support): Customer impact: several requests that should've been soft-failed (429) triggered end-user retries and billing confusion. They saw 12 failed job runs in CI. Need a short-term rollback/mitigation.

Dana (CXS): I'll draft the customer message. We should confirm mitigation plan first. They want guaranteed 429 semantics for rate limiting.

Alex (SRE): Mitigation options:
- Temporarily change gateway to map dependency timeouts for quota-service -> return 429 when quota decision is absent due to timeout (safe backstop).
- Increase quota-service dependency timeout + scale up instances for today.
- Add a circuit-breaker/hard-fail path that returns 429 for auth-deny flows if classifier fails.

oncall-sre: I can push a config toggle to gate that mapping now. Low-risk patch: on dependency timeout interpret as "quota decision: deny" with 429. Will monitor for false positives.

Marco (Runtime): Before we flip anything, here's a quick repro that I can run against staging to verify behavior:
```bash
# flood with concurrent requests to hit quota path and force timeout
seq 1 200 | xargs -n1 -P50 -I{} curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} ' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  -d '{"input":"spam"}' https://staging-api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?model=gpt-medium
```
Expect: mostly 200/429, not 5xx.

Marco (Runtime): I reproduced the 502s in staging when I artificially injected a 1s latency to quota-service and reduced its connections. The mapping code path (classifier that converts internal reason->HTTP) failed for reasons flagged in logs (null rule for 'auth_denied_revoked_token').

Priya (Support): Customer also reported that this spike coincided with a token refresh window for their clients. Could be auth-deny variant.

Dana (CXS): Prioritize stable mapping fix. Customer-facing message ready once we confirm mitigation.

Alex (SRE): Action plan (short):
1) oncall-sre to toggle backstop mapping now to stop 5xx -> 429 for timeouts. (ETA 10m)
2) Marco to deploy hotfix to mapping rules to include 'auth_denied_revoked_token' and resilience around null classifier. (ETA 1-2h)
3) Scale quota-service by +20% for next 6h to reduce timeouts.
4) Postmortem and billing review — we may credit customer's failed runs.

oncall-sre: toggled backstop mapping at 09:41Z. Monitoring: 502s for the sample req id dropped to 0 in the last 5m.

Marco (Runtime): pushing mapping rule now to include the missing classifier entry and adding defensive default that returns 429 for unknown deny reasons. Deploying to prod canary.

deploy-bot: [deploy] started rollout: quota-gateway/mapping-fix v2026.3.15-hotfix -> canary 2/10 hosts

Marco (Runtime): canary shows correct behavior: for forced latency tests we now get 429 instead of 502. Logs show classifier hit.

Priya (Support): Customer notified of temporary mitigation and that we have a hotfix in canary. They asked for timeline for full rollout.

Alex (SRE): scale-up completed (+25% instances) at 10:05Z. Latency metrics for quota-service improved.

Dana (CXS): Sent customer note: "We've applied a mitigation to ensure quota/timeouts return 429 semantics and deployed a fix to mapping rules; monitoring indicates the issue is mitigated. We'll follow up with a formal postmortem and potential credits."

Priya (Support): Customer responded: thank you, confirmed failures stopped. Will reopen if anything reappears. :thumbsup:

Marco (Runtime): I'll keep an eye on rollout and push full prod if no regressions in 30m. Also creating PR for improved unit tests around classifier defaults.

Alex (SRE): Marking incident as active -> mitigated. Creating follow-up items: INC-2026-POSTMORTEM, billing-impact, tests+observability.

Dana (CXS): I'll coordinate the billing review and customer follow-up.

Priya (Support): closing loop with customer in 1hr when full prod rollout completes.

Alex (SRE): Good ops. Thanks everyone.
